defaults.question: Registry MCP server, or a CLI over JSONL files?
defaults.taken: CLI over JSONL; no MCP server
defaults.alt: SQLite registry MCP server (12 Sept brief, Phase 2)
defaults.reason: A JSONL fold is enough below a few hundred items, beads' storage change broke its tooling, and the Artifact board already spans clients without an MCP app.

defaults.question: Capture with a model classifier on every Stop, or with agent markers?
defaults.taken: Agent-emitted markers read by command hooks, zero model tokens
defaults.alt: Prompt hook classifier on every Stop
defaults.reason: Prompt hooks call a model on every firing; Codex's automatic recaps drew complaints about hidden cost and mislabelled status.

defaults.question: Hide every recommendation behind a reveal, or pre-select it when earned?
defaults.taken: Pre-select only when earned; options first for one-way or unstable items
defaults.alt: Reveal on demand for every item (12 Sept brief, principle 6)
defaults.reason: Pre-selected defaults stay strong whether disclosed or not, a bare verdict drew the lowest agreement, and options-first display costs about seven times the decision time.

decided.question: Which runtime should the standalone Weigh-In CLI use, now that redkiln-rs is its eventual home?
decided.why: The CLI is the single writer of the ledger and the piece redkiln-rs will absorb. Writing it in redkiln-rs's language decides whether integration adopts code or re-implements it.
decided.door_note: A small CLI can be rewritten, but every week on the wrong runtime adds code that is thrown away at integration.
decided.resolve_by: before slice 1 starts (it is the first line of code)
decided.reopen_note: redkiln has a newer version (redkiln-rs), written in Rust, which is still in active development. This will be the eventual home of the weigh-in system - but it needs to be able to stand on it's own until redkiln-rs is ready to receive it
decided.timing: Decide now. Slice 1 cannot start without it, and the only unknown (whether a prebuilt binary runs in each surface) is a 20-minute spike that the recommendation already schedules.

source.quote: Node 20 or later, one dependency-free file

evidence.text: redkiln-rs will be the eventual home of Weigh-In; Weigh-In must stand on its own until then.
Rust, edition 2024, rust-version 1.98.1, pinned exactly in rust-toolchain.toml.
happenstance 0.3.2 (your DCB event store, MSRV 1.97.1) is proposed as redkiln-rs's tier-2 store adapter, with git staying the tier-1 authority.
redkiln-rs reads git through gix and shells out for every git write, the same split a Weigh-In CLI needs.
Cowork cannot install a plugin's bin/ executables; a binary inside a skill folder run through Bash is unverified.
Your box runs core.autocrlf=true; redkiln-rs forces LF in every checkout, so whatever writes ledger files must write LF.

options.title: Rust crate and CLI on redkiln-rs's toolchain
options.summary: A weighin-core crate plus a weighin binary, pinned to Rust 1.98.1, edition 2024, events stored through happenstance. Prebuilt binaries for Windows x64 and Linux x64 ship in the plugin. Cowork, which has no repo, keeps its ledger in the board's store and needs no binary.
options.holds_if: a prebuilt binary runs from the plugin folder on Windows and in Claude Code cloud sessions (20-minute spike)
options.if_wrong: you maintain release builds for two targets for a small tool; the core crate is still what redkiln-rs adopts

options.title: Node single file now, port to Rust at integration
options.summary: The original default: one dependency-free Node file, run the same way everywhere Node runs.
options.holds_if: the data contract, not the code, is what carries into redkiln-rs
options.if_wrong: about 1,500 lines written twice, and two implementations of the ID and fold rules while both are live

options.title: Rust core compiled to WebAssembly behind a Node shim
options.summary: One .wasm artifact runs wherever Node runs; the same crate links natively into redkiln-rs.
options.holds_if: the shared logic is pure: git and process calls stay in the shim
options.if_wrong: git, rg and file watching live in JavaScript anyway, splitting the logic you meant to share; node:wasi is still experimental

recommendation.flip: The spike shows a prebuilt binary will not run from a plugin in Claude Code cloud sessions or on your Windows install. Then B, keeping the event schema identical so the port is mechanical.
recommendation.tradeoff: You are trading release plumbing for two targets for code that redkiln-rs adopts rather than rewrites.
recommendation.why_wrong: redkiln-rs's own ports may change shape before integration. A crate written now against happenstance may still need an adapter, so adopting the crate could shrink to adopting its data.

decided.question: Where should Weigh-In keep its live ledger so that moving into redkiln-rs later adds no source-control friction?
decided.why: redkiln-rs keeps git as the authority for decisions and a derived store outside the working tree. A Weigh-In ledger committed as files would be a second shape that redkiln-rs has to import or ignore.
decided.door_note: Ledger files already pushed to your repos stay in history; everything else can move.
decided.reopen_note: redkiln-rs works slightly differently in terms of it's approach to git. weigh-in needs to stand on it's own until redkiln-rs is ready to integrate it - but we should anticipate that merge and ensure that we do not create friction from a source control perspective
decided.supersedes: wi-a93f02 (commit event files in your repos), on the redkiln-rs evidence below
decided.timing: Decide now. Every session run before this is settled writes ledger files in whichever shape slice 1 ships.

source.quote: One event file per session, ordered by lamport, timestamp and event id

evidence.text: redkiln-rs keeps one store per repository at <git-common-dir>/redkiln/store.sqlite3, shared by every worktree and never committed.
Rows are keyed by SHA or tree hash, never branch or path; rebase and amend emit rewrite events; only the run-owned worktree writes.
An answer is recorded as a trailer commit on the run's branch, with the tree hash taken from a temporary index (untracked files excluded).
git stays the tier-1 authority; the store is derived and rebuildable. F19 rebuilt 174 of 174 records from git.
In Phase 1 only a CLI answer reconciles; a web view is not an answer channel. Board answers must therefore be applied by the CLI, as Weigh-In already does.
You chose C: commit event files in your repos, keep them local in client repos. This card would supersede the committing half.

lines: /// **One store per repository** (AC-178). Resolved from the common dir, which on arm a's **go** is
/// what gix reports from any worktree — so opening from a linked worktree yields the main
/// repository's store rather than a second one beside it.

options.title: Mirror redkiln-rs: git for decisions, a common-dir store for open items
options.summary: Open items live in <git-common-dir>/weighin/, shared by every worktree and never committed. Decisions reach git as .kb/_intake atoms plus a Weigh-In trailer on the enacting commit. Your repos mirror open items to the board for other machines.
options.holds_if: you never need undecided items from a fresh clone of a client repo
options.if_wrong: open items in client repos stay on one machine, as wi-7c21e4 already accepts; a lost clone loses open items not yet decided

options.title: Keep committed per-session event files (wi-a93f02 as decided)
options.summary: Event files under .kb/_ledger/events in your repos; write an importer into redkiln-rs's store at integration.
options.holds_if: redkiln-rs is happy to import and then ignore those files
options.if_wrong: your repos carry ledger history redkiln-rs never reads, and two ledgers drift apart while both run

options.title: Commit open items as open_question atoms; no store
options.summary: Every open item is an atom in .kb/_intake from the moment it is raised; git holds everything.
options.holds_if: open items change status rarely
options.if_wrong: each triage, defer and default becomes a commit, and kb-ingest's handling of frequently changing open_question atoms is still unverified

recommendation.flip: You want open items visible to other people or to CI in a shared repo. Then keep A and add a committed export on demand.
recommendation.tradeoff: You are trading open items in git history for a ledger with the same shape redkiln-rs will absorb.
recommendation.why_wrong: A trusts the board for cross-machine continuity. If the board is off for a repo (client repos), a cloud session there starts with no open items, which is a real regression from B for client work.

decided.question: May Weigh-In publish ledger items from IQBG client repos to a claude.ai Artifact board?
decided.why: Board items quote client code, requirements and your deliberations. The board keeps them on claude.ai, visible to your organisation, long after the session that raised them.
decided.door_note: Published excerpts can be deleted but not un-seen; a breach of client terms cannot be undone.
decided.timing: Decide now. The fact that would flip this (each client's terms on Anthropic as a subprocessor) is knowable per engagement today; waiting will not reveal it.

source.quote: May ledger items from IQBG client repos be published to a claude.ai Artifact board?

evidence.text: Artifacts need a claude.ai login and the Anthropic API (not Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry), and are unavailable in CMEK, HIPAA or ZDR organisations.
A board with a db store is organisation-internal and cannot be shared publicly. Any viewer can write the store, so answers read back are treated as untrusted.
Claude Code already sends the code in context to Anthropic during a session. The board adds persistence and an org-visible surface, not new processing.
Records land in the same .kb layout everywhere, so the ledger stays in the repo whatever the board mode.

options.title: Per-repo board mode; client repos default to local
options.summary: board: artifact | local | off in .kb/_ledger/config.json. Wet Ink and Redkiln repos use the Artifact board; client repos use the local page and in-chat cards until you switch one.
options.holds_if: you can say at init whether a repo belongs to a client
options.if_wrong: one extra setting per repo; a client repo you would have allowed runs without the board until switched

options.title: Artifact board in every repo
options.summary: One surface everywhere, including client repos, reachable from Cowork, the desktop app and your phone.
options.holds_if: every client's terms already allow Anthropic to process and store excerpts of their code
options.if_wrong: client excerpts persisted on claude.ai against their terms, beyond recall from anyone who viewed them

options.title: No hosted board anywhere
options.summary: Local review page and in-chat cards only, in every repo including your own.
options.holds_if: you never need the board from Cowork, away from your machine, or on your phone
options.if_wrong: you lose the only surface that spans Claude Code and Cowork, for your own repos too

recommendation.flip: IQBG's standard client terms name Anthropic as an approved subprocessor for code excerpts. Then B for those clients.
recommendation.tradeoff: You are trading one uniform surface for a per-repo setting.
recommendation.why_wrong: If every IQBG engagement already runs Claude Code under terms that cover Anthropic, the board's extra exposure is persistence and org visibility only, and the per-repo friction buys little.

decided.question: Should the ledger's event files (.kb/_ledger/events) be committed to git?
decided.why: Committed events travel with branches, pull requests and machines. They also put raw agent deliberation into repo history, which a client may not want in theirs.
decided.door_note: You can stop committing at any time, but files already pushed stay in history.
decided.resolve_by: before slice 1 ships (weighin init needs a default)
decided.timing: Decide now. init needs a default, and a per-repo override keeps it cheap to revisit.

evidence.text: Redkiln already commits append-only JSONL telemetry, one partition per actor@worktree.
auto_stage_telemetry: Redkiln stages those partitions with git add by default.
The repo view folds events across git worktree list, so open items are visible across worktrees whether or not events are committed.
Claude Code cloud sessions clone from the remote; an uncommitted ledger does not exist there.

lines: * Events are append-only JSONL, one object per line, written to a per-actor /
* record is validated against the `Event` schema before it is appended, so the
* on-disk log always round-trips through the schema.

options.title: Commit by default; opt out per repo
options.summary: Every repo commits its event files; a repo that must not carry agent metadata excludes them with .git/info/exclude.
options.holds_if: most repos you work in tolerate agent metadata in history
options.if_wrong: an opted-in client repo carries ledger files in pushed history; removing them needs a history rewrite

options.title: Never commit; only decided atoms reach git
options.summary: Event files stay local and gitignored everywhere; the curated .kb atoms are the only committed record.
options.holds_if: you work from one machine and never need open items in a cloud session or on a PR
options.if_wrong: open items vanish on other machines and in cloud sessions; a lost clone loses the open ledger

options.title: Commit in your repos; client repos local by default

options.holds_if: one own/client flag at init describes your repos well enough
options.if_wrong: client repos lose open items in cloud sessions and across machines until you opt in

criteria.name: Open items follow you across machines

values.C: One flag, shared with the board

recommendation.flip: Your client engagements treat decision records as a deliverable they want in their repos. Then A.
recommendation.tradeoff: You are trading cloud-session continuity in client repos for keeping raw deliberation out of client history.
recommendation.why_wrong: The decided atoms already land in client repos. If clients are fine with those, the raw events add little extra exposure and C costs you continuity for nothing.

decided.question: May unattended runs decide two-way, judgment-bound questions themselves and report them in a digest?
decided.why: About half your agent work runs unattended. Without a rule, those runs either stall on every question or make silent assumptions, which are the buried questions this skill exists to surface.
decided.door_note: Any default can be reopened from the digest; reopening supersedes it.
decided.timing: Decide now. Nothing arrives by waiting; the digest's override rate will show later whether to tighten.

source.quote: May unattended runs auto-decide two-way, judgment-bound items and report them in the digest?

evidence.text: Your agent work is about half interactive, half unattended.
"With no usable blocking-question tool, behave as non-interactive"; only authority-bound items are escalated to the human.
AskUserQuestion is unavailable to subagents and in claude -p runs.
Two-way-door decisions "can and should be made quickly by high judgment individuals or small groups".

options.title: Yes for two-way items; one-way items block
options.summary: Unattended runs take a logged default on two-way, judgment-bound items and list it in the digest. One-way items are marked did: blocked and the run continues with independent work.
options.holds_if: runs classify door type correctly most of the time
options.if_wrong: a misclassified one-way item gets a default; the digest shows it and a reopen supersedes it

options.title: No; every item waits for you
options.summary: Unattended runs park each question until you answer, using the SDK defer loop.
options.holds_if: unattended runs can wait hours for you
options.if_wrong: runs stall, and the slice 3 defer loop becomes a prerequisite for slice 1

options.title: Yes for every item, one-way included
options.summary: Unattended runs decide everything and report it all in the digest.
options.holds_if: you are willing to review one-way calls after the fact
options.if_wrong: an irreversible choice is made with nobody asked
options.fails_must: One-way doors always get a human (principle 1 of the 12 September brief)

recommendation.flip: The slice 1 eval shows the unattended door classifier calling one-way items two-way more than about 1 in 20 times. Then B for those repos until it improves.
recommendation.tradeoff: You are trading a small chance of a misclassified default for runs that finish.
recommendation.why_wrong: Door classification is the weak link. If the unattended run misjudges one-way items often, A drifts into C by accident; the slice 1 eval must measure that miss rate before you rely on it.

decided.question: Should Redkiln's .kb contract reserve .kb/_ledger/ and accept Weigh-In's intake keys in slice 1?
decided.why: Decides whether every repo has one .kb footprint from day one, and whether the later native decision type is a mapping or a migration.
decided.door_note: A contract note and a kb-ingest change; both can be revised.
decided.timing: Decide now. Waiting for slice 3 adds a migration of every ledger written in the meantime.

source.quote: Reserve .kb/_ledger/ in Redkiln's .kb contract and teach validate --kb and kb-ingest the Weigh-In intake keys?

evidence.text: validate --kb already skips _-prefixed directories, so .kb/_ledger/ is invisible to atom validation today.
KbFrontmatter is .passthrough(), so Weigh-In keys such as weighin_item, door and flip_condition survive validation without a schema change.
The schema comment already names tracks and resolution_ref as keys seen on open_question atoms.
Same .kb layout everywhere.
How kb-ingest handles open_question atoms whose status changes often is unverified.

options.title: Yes: reserve it and teach kb-ingest now
options.summary: Document .kb/_ledger/ as reserved in the .kb README and teach kb-ingest the intake keys in slice 1.
options.holds_if: the key names survive slice 1 use without much churn
options.if_wrong: a key rename touches the README and kb-ingest, not stored atoms (passthrough keeps them valid)

options.title: Own .weighin/ folder until slice 3
options.summary: Keep the ledger outside .kb until the native decision type lands, then move it.

decided.question: Should Weigh-In run reliance drills, occasionally marking a deliberately weaker option as recommended, to check that you still review?
decided.why: You expect to accept the recommendation most of the time. Pre-selected defaults are strong and disclosure does not weaken them, so an unmeasured rubber stamp is the main way this skill could make your decisions worse.
decided.door_note: Drills can be switched off at any sitting.
decided.timing: Decide now. Nothing will arrive to change this except your own override rate, which every option already measures.

evidence.text: Defaults shift choices with an overall effect of d = 0.68 across 58 studies; perceived endorsement is one of the moderators.
Disclosing a default does not weaken it.
Human–AI teams did worse than the better of the two on decision tasks (g = −0.23, 106 studies).
Options-first deliberative display raised accuracy from 52.4% to 59.8% but median time per decision from 33 s to 236 s.

options.title: Yes, two-way items only, 1 in 30 for 60 days
options.summary: A drill marks a weaker option as recommended on a two-way item and is disclosed before the sitting writes anything back.
options.holds_if: one extra careful look per 30 items is worth a measured check on your review habit
options.if_wrong: mild annoyance; a missed drill is reverted before write-back, so nothing wrong is recorded

options.title: No drills; watch override rate and time-to-decide
options.summary: Trust the metrics every sitting already records.
options.holds_if: override rate and time-to-decide are enough signal that you still review
options.if_wrong: a rubber-stamp habit goes unseen, because a low override rate looks the same as good recommendations

options.title: Never pre-select; options first on every item
options.summary: Show options and evidence before any recommendation, on every item.
options.holds_if: you accept roughly seven times longer per decision
options.if_wrong: every sitting slows down, and the habit of running /weigh-in erodes

recommendation.flip: Your override rate in the first 60 items is above about 15%. That already shows active review, so B.
recommendation.tradeoff: You are trading a rare moment of friction for evidence that your acceptances are real reviews.
recommendation.why_wrong: The evidence for drills is one study in a different setting. For a single expert reviewing his own architecture, a drill may feel like noise and cost more trust in the tool than it earns.
